say: DO: rename the config key to retry_limit everywhere, docs included.
does: Checks it won't break anything, then makes the change.

say: CONSIDER: is the no-network rule in our tests still earning its keep? I suspect recorded fixtures would catch more.
does: Argues both sides and pushes back if you're wrong. Any change it wants, it proposes in writing. Your files stay put.

say: 1. Ship the parser fix and commit. 2. CONSIDER: moving the slow nightly sources onto their own schedule.
does: Ships and commits item 1. Gives you a written take on item 2. A marker covers only what it tags.

say: DO: sketch three designs for the import flow. Plan only, build nothing yet.
does: Writes up three designs and edits nothing. When a message limits its own scope, the limit wins.

say: TRY(coldread:) rewrite the install section, then have a fresh agent follow it cold.
does: Drafts it in scratch and hands it to a reviewer with no context. Keeps it only if it clears that read.

say: TRY(yourcall:) the CLI's error messages read curt. Soften them if you think it helps.
does: Makes the call either way, then leaves a three-line receipt saying how it read you and why.

say: TRY(showme:) a dark-mode version of the settings page.
does: Builds it in scratch and shows you the real thing. You keep it or toss it.

say: learn: staging resets every Sunday night, so Monday-morning row counts mean nothing.
does: Says it back in its own words and flags gaps. Acts on nothing.
